knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Projection Scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projected subgradient method with an exactly evaluated metric projection onto a closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. Given \(x_0\in C\), positive stepsizes \((\alpha_k)\), and a limit \(T\), choose \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and compute \[x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_kg_k),\qquad P_C(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\frac12\lVert z-y\rVert_2^2.\] Stop early if \(0\in\partial f(x_k)+N_C(x_k)\); otherwise, after \(T\) iterations return the declared best iterate or weighted average. Exact projection means that the displayed minimization is solved to global optimality at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take a subgradient step and then compute the exact Euclidean nearest feasible point; stop at a constrained first-order stationary point or return the declared aggregate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(x_0\in C\).
\(f\) is proper and convex with a subgradient available at each iterate.

notation.meaning: exact Euclidean projection onto the feasible set
convex-analytic normal cone to the feasible set at x

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Projection Scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient iteration whose Euclidean projection subproblem is solved with a certified additive objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Given \(x_0\in C\), stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), projection tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), and limit \(T\), choose \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), set \(y_k=x_k-\alpha_kg_k\), and choose \(x_{k+1}\in C\) satisfying \[\frac12\lVert x_{k+1}-y_k\rVert_2^2\le \inf_{z\in C}\frac12\lVert z-y_k\rVert_2^2+\varepsilon_k.\] Stop if a declared constrained optimality test holds; otherwise return the declared best iterate or weighted average after \(T\) iterations. The case \(\varepsilon_k=0\) reduces to exact Euclidean projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each subgradient step, return a feasible point whose squared-distance projection objective is within a prescribed additive tolerance of its optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(x_0\in C\).
\(f\) is proper and convex with \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(x_{k+1}\) is feasible and satisfies the displayed additive projection-error certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Additive projection-objective error is one particular inexact-projection convention and is not determined by the node title. An authoritative source is required to support this exact certificate and algorithmic variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Projection Scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric projected subgradient method using uniformly positive-definite scaling matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Given \(x_0\in C\), stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), symmetric positive-definite matrices \(H_k\), and limit \(T\), choose \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and compute \[x_{k+1}=P_C^{H_k}(x_k-\alpha_kH_k^{-1}g_k),\qquad P_C^{H}(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\frac12\lVert z-y\rVert_H^2.\] Require uniform spectral bounds \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\). Stop at a declared constrained optimality test; otherwise return the declared best iterate or weighted average after \(T\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precondition the subgradient by a positive-definite matrix and project exactly in the corresponding weighted norm, with scaling matrices uniformly bounded above and below.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is the exact \(H_k\)-metric projection of \(x_k-\alpha_kH_k^{-1}g_k\) onto \(C\).

notation.meaning: weighted norm defined by the square root of v-transpose-H-v
projection onto C in the H metric

knowledge_statements.title: Constant Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed positive stepsize assignment for all iterations of a subgradient method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constant stepsize policy chooses a scalar \(\alpha>0\) before iteration and imposes \[\alpha_k=\alpha\qquad\text{for every }k\ge0.\] For a normalized subgradient update \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k/\lVert g_k\rVert_2)\), the same definition applies to the step length \(\alpha_k\); for an unnormalized update \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), it applies to the multiplier of \(g_k\). The selected convention must remain fixed throughout the run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one positive step parameter and use it at every iteration, while explicitly fixing whether it multiplies a raw or normalized subgradient.
assumptions_latex: A raw-subgradient or normalized-subgradient update convention has been fixed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Constant Stepsizes for the Finite-Horizon Bound Proxy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization of the finite-horizon scalar proxy arising in the subgradient-method error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let N\ge 1 be an integer and R>0. For h_0,\ldots,h_N>0, define \Delta_N(h_0,\ldots,h_N)=\frac{R^2+\sum_{i=0}^N h_i^2}{2\sum_{i=0}^N h_i}. Then \Delta_N attains its minimum over (0,\infty)^{N+1} at h_i=\frac{R}{\sqrt{N+1}} for every i=0,\ldots,N, and the minimum value is \frac{R}{\sqrt{N+1}}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among all positive steps over a horizon of N+1 steps, the stated bound proxy is minimized by choosing every step equal to R divided by the square root of N+1. Its minimum is the same quantity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-Stepsize Subgradient Near-Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded asymptotic objective guarantee and iterate-convergence boundary for a constant subgradient step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f$ be convex and let $S^*=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing$, with optimal value $f^*$. For every $\delta>0$, there exists $r>0$ such that, if Algorithm 14.3.1 uses $\alpha_k\equiv\alpha\in(0,r)$, then $\liminf_{k\to\infty}f(x_k)\leq f^*+\delta$. This objective-value guarantee does not guarantee convergence of the iterate sequence; a constant stepsize may cause the iterates not to converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any positive objective tolerance, a sufficiently small positive constant step length makes the liminf objective value lie within that tolerance of optimality. The result does not ensure convergence of the iterates, which may fail under a constant step length.

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Monro-type diminishing stepsizes for deterministic convex subgradient convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A square-summable but nonsummable diminishing stepsize policy is a deterministic sequence \((\alpha_k)_{k\ge0}\) satisfying \[\alpha_k>0,\qquad \alpha_k\to0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty.\] A standard power-law instance is \(\alpha_k=a/(k+1)^p\) with \(a>0\) and \(1/2<p\le1\). This condition is attached to the multiplier of the raw subgradient in the projected or unprojected subgradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use positive steps that vanish, have infinite total length, and have finite squared total length; power laws with exponent above one-half and at most one qualify.
assumptions_latex: The stepsizes are deterministic positive scalars.
The update multiplies the raw subgradient by \(\alpha_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Tuned Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant stepsize tuned to a known iteration horizon for Lipschitz convex minimization over a bounded-distance domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), and suppose \(\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2\le R\) and every selected subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\le G\). For a known horizon \(T\ge1\), run projected subgradient descent with \[\alpha_k=\frac{R}{G\sqrt{T}}\qquad(0\le k<T)\] and return \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}x_k\). Then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt{T}}.\] Thus \(T\ge(RG/\varepsilon)^2\) suffices for objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a known horizon, choose the constant step R divided by G times the square root of T; the averaged iterate has objective error at most RG divided by the square root of T.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and attains its minimum over nonempty closed convex \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le RG/\sqrt{T}\), so the iteration complexity is \(O(R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2)\).

notation.meaning: upper bound on initial distance to an optimizer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and best-value rate for projected subgradient with Polyak stepsizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific convergence theorem under the extraction's referenced projected-subgradient assumptions and uniform subgradient boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumptions 8.7 and 8.12 hold, and let \(\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\) be generated by the projected subgradient method with the Polyak stepsize rule. Then, for every \(k\geq0\) and \(x^*\in X^*\),
\[
\|x^{k+1}-x^*\|^2\leq\|x^k-x^*\|^2.
\]
Moreover, \(f(x^k)\to f_{\mathrm{opt}}\), and, for every \(k\geq0\),
\[
f_{\mathrm{best}}^k-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{L_f d_{x^*}(x^0)}{\sqrt{k+1}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 8.7 and 8.12, projected subgradient iterates using the Polyak stepsize do not increase their distance to any optimizer, their objective values converge to the optimum, and their best objective gap satisfies the stated inverse-square-root bound.
assumptions_latex: \exists L_f>0\;\forall x\in C\;\forall g\in\partial f(x),\ \|g\|\leq L_f
\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by the projected subgradient method with the Polyak stepsize rule}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\geq0\;\forall x^*\in X^*,\ \|x^{k+1}-x^*\|^2\leq\|x^k-x^*\|^2;\quad f(x^k)\to f_{\mathrm{opt}};\quad \forall k\geq0,\ f_{\mathrm{best}}^k-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{L_f d_{x^*}(x^0)}{\sqrt{k+1}}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyak subgradient steps using the known attained optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), assume the attained value \(f^*=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) is known, and start from \(x_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). If \(f(x_k)=f^*\), stop and return \(x_k\). If \(g_k\ne0\), choose a relaxation \(\gamma_k\in(0,2)\), set \[\alpha_k=

\alpha_kg_k),\] and continue until the declared iteration limit, then return the best objective iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyak stepsize with known optimal value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-target Polyak stepsize rule, including the extraction's convention for a zero selected subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the optimal value \(f_{\mathrm{opt}}\) and a selected subgradient \(f'(x^k)\), set
\[
t_k=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{f(x^k)-f_{\mathrm{opt}}}{\|f'(x^k)\|^2},&f'(x^k)\neq0,\\
1,&f'(x^k)=0.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At iteration k, divide the current objective gap by the squared norm of the selected subgradient when that subgradient is nonzero. If it is zero, set the stepsize to one.
assumptions_latex: f'(x^k)\in\partial f(x^k)\text{ is the selected subgradient}

knowledge_statements.title: Estimated-Target Policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyak-type steps formed with a supplied target value in place of the unknown optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), fix a target \(\tau\in\mathbb R\), and initialize \(x_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). If \(f(x_k)\le	au\), stop and return \(x_k\). Otherwise, if \(g_k\ne0\), choose \(\gamma_kin(0,2)\) and set \[\alpha_k=
\gamma_k\frac{f(x_k)-	au}{\lVert g_k\rVert_2^2},\qquad x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-
\alpha_kg_k).\] Continue to the declared iteration limit and return the best objective iterate if the target has not been reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the unknown optimum in the Polyak formula by a fixed target; stop when the objective reaches that target, otherwise return the best iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on nonempty closed convex \(C\), and \(x_0\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
While \(f(x_k)>	au\), the method uses \(\alpha_k=
\gamma_k(f(x_k)-	au)/\lVert g_k\rVert_2^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this particular fixed-target variant, and the statement contains malformed TeX in \gamma_kin(0,2). The admissible relation of the target to the optimum and the intended guarantees also require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Target-Value Policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-based Polyak policy that lowers its target after successful level attainment or unsuccessful phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an initial level \(L_0<f(x_0)\), decrements \(\delta_j>0\), phase budgets \(B_j\in\mathbb N\), and relaxations \(\gamma_k\in(0,2)\). During phase \(j\), use the target \(\tau_j=L_j-
\delta_j\) and, while \(f(x_k)>	au_j\), update \[\alpha_k=
\gamma_k\frac{f(x_k)-	au_j}{\lVert g_k\rVert_2^2},\qquad x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-
\alpha_kg_k).\] If an iterate satisfies \(f(x_k)\le	au_j\), set \(L_{j+1}=f(x_k)\); if \(B_j\) phase iterations expire first, set \(L_{j+1}=L_j\). In either case, select a new positive decrement and begin the next phase. Return the incumbent with smallest objective value at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run Polyak steps against a phase target below the incumbent level, then revise the level and decrement after reaching the target or exhausting the phase budget.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on nonempty closed convex \(C\), and nonzero subgradients are available above each target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Each phase uses target \(\tau_j=L_j-
\delta_j\) and updates the level according to target attainment before starting another phase.

notation.meaning: incumbent objective level at phase j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Adaptive level methods have materially different phase, decrement, budget, and restart rules. No source is supplied for this particular construction, so its exact algorithm cannot be validated.

knowledge_statements.title: Doubling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic horizon-doubling wrapper for converting a horizon-tuned subgradient routine into an anytime procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A(H,z)\) be a base routine initialized at \(z\) and configured for exactly \(H\) oracle calls. Choose \(H_0\in\mathbb N\), set \(z_0=x_0\), and for epochs \(j=0,1,2,\ldots\) set \(H_j=2^jH_0\), run \(y_j=\mathcal A(H_j,z_j)\), record \(y_j\), and set \(z_{j+1}=y_j\). Stop when the cumulative oracle-call budget is exhausted and return the recorded point having the smallest observed objective value. If the final epoch has insufficient remaining budget, run its valid truncated form or return the best point from completed epochs, as fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a horizon-dependent base method in epochs whose lengths double, warm-start each epoch from the preceding output, and return the best recorded point.
assumptions_latex: The base routine \(\mathcal A(H,z)\) is defined for every integer horizon \(H\ge H_0\).
Objective values at recorded epoch outputs are available for selecting the incumbent.
The treatment of an incomplete final epoch is declared before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Epoch \(j\) has horizon \(H_j=2^jH_0\), and the returned point is the best recorded epoch output.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed warm-started horizon-doubling wrapper is plausible but is not uniquely determined by the title. Its restart state, output selection, and incomplete-epoch conventions require a supporting source.

children.title: Restart Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies that relaunch a subgradient schedule from a revised operating regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic epochwise restart wrapper for a projected subgradient method with geometrically enlarged scale estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), an initial point \(x^{(0)}\in C\), an initial scale \(R_0>0\), and an epoch budget rule \(T_j\), set \(R_j=2^jR_0\). During epoch \(j\), run a projected subgradient method from \(x^{(j)}\) for at most \(T_j\) iterations using the scale-dependent stepsize rule \(\alpha_{j,t}=\alpha_t(R_j)>0\). If the prescribed restart trigger occurs, terminate the epoch, choose its designated output \(\widehat x_j\in C\), and initialize the next epoch by \(x^{(j+1)}=\widehat x_j\). Otherwise return \(\widehat x_j\). After a finite global budget, return the designated output of the last completed epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run subgradient epochs under a current scale estimate, double that estimate when a trigger fires, and restart from the preceding epoch’s designated output.
assumptions_latex: Each epoch uses a well-defined projected subgradient update and a finite budget \(T_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{j+1}=2R_j\) at every triggered restart, and every epoch initialization and returned output belongs to \(C\).

notation.meaning: scale estimate used in epoch j

review_flags: Exact restart trigger and epoch-output conventions vary across parameter-free subgradient methods.
REQUEST_SOURCES: no supplied locator specifically documents the doubling-restart wrapper.

children.title: Restart Trigger Regimes
children.top_down_role: Observable events or phase criteria used to initiate restarts.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Trigger Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable trigger predicates for epochwise scale-doubling subgradient policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let epoch \(j\) start at \(x^{(j)}\), use scale estimate \(R_j>0\), and generate iterates \(x_{j,0},x_{j,1},\ldots\) with observed subgradients \(g_{j,t}\). A restart-trigger regime is a sequence of predicates \(\tau_{j,t}\in\{0,1\}\), each measurable with respect to the history through time \(t\). The epoch stops at \(\sigma_j=\inf\{t\geq 0:\tau_{j,t}=1\}\). Typical admissible regimes include a fixed-budget trigger \(\tau_{j,t}=\mathbf 1\{t=T_j\}\), a radius trigger \(\tau_{j,t}=\mathbf 1\{\|x_{j,t}-x^{(j)}\|>R_j\}\), and an accumulated-scale trigger \(\tau_{j,t}=\mathbf 1\{\sum_{s=0}^{t}\alpha_{j,s}\|g_{j,s}\|>R_j\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart time is the first history-measurable event indicating that an epoch budget, displacement bound, or accumulated subgradient scale has been exceeded.
assumptions_latex: The trigger uses only information observed by the end of the current iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_j\) is a stopping time for the epoch history and determines whether and when the scale is enlarged.

notation.meaning: first triggered iteration in epoch j

review_flags: The displayed regimes are generic formalizations rather than a uniquely identified named policy.
REQUEST_SOURCES: a source fixing the intended trigger family is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the Restart Trigger Regimes leaf, and the stopping-time formalization is coherent. However, no source supports the asserted collection of fixed-budget, radius, and accumulated-scale triggers as the intended family; the last two formulas are policy-specific rather than canonical consequences of the parent container.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Dependent Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar cumulative-subgradient stepsizes for Euclidean projected subgradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing a convex function \(f\) over a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), choose \(x_1\in C\), \(D>0\), and \(\delta>0\). At iteration \(t\), obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), form \(S_t=\delta^2+\sum_{s=1}^{t}\|g_s\|^2\), set \(\alpha_t=D/\sqrt{S_t}\), and update \[x_{t+1}=P_C(x_t-\alpha_t g_t).\] After \(T\) iterations, return either a specified iterate or the weighted average \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha_t x_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha_t)\). Thus each stepsize is determined by observed subgradient magnitudes rather than a preassigned Lipschitz bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale each projected subgradient step by the inverse square root of the cumulative observed squared subgradient norms.
assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and subdifferentiable at every generated iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_t>0\) is history-measurable and nonincreasing, and \(x_{t+1}\in C\) for every \(t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Projected Subgradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-unbiased stochastic subgradient iteration for constrained convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\). Choose \(x_1\in C\) and positive stepsizes \((\alpha_t)\). At iteration \(t\), sample \(\xi_t\), compute a stochastic subgradient \(G_t\), and update \[x_{t+1}=P_C(x_t-\alpha_tG_t).\] With \(\mathcal F_t\) denoting the information available before sampling \(\xi_t\), require \(\mathbb{E}[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|G_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]<\infty\). After \(T\) oracle calls, return the prescribed last, best, or averaged iterate in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each iterate after stepping along a conditionally unbiased stochastic subgradient of the expected convex objective.
assumptions_latex: The stochastic oracle is conditionally unbiased and has finite conditional second moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in C\) for all \(t\), and the conditional mean search direction belongs to \(\partial f(x_t)\).

notation.meaning: stochastic subgradient returned at iteration t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic projection-based stochastic subgradient update on a feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient-Inequality Representation of Conditional Unbiasedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent inequality representation of the conditional-mean subgradient condition used by the stochastic method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(k\ge0\), the condition
\[
\mathbb{E}(\mathbf{g}^k\mid\mathbf{x}^k)\in\partial f(\mathbf{x}^k)
\]
can equivalently be written as
\[
f(\mathbf z)\ge f(\mathbf{x}^k)+\left\langle\mathbb{E}(\mathbf{g}^k\mid\mathbf{x}^k),\mathbf z-\mathbf{x}^k\right\rangle
\quad\text{for every }\mathbf z\in\operatorname{dom}(f).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional expectation of the stochastic direction is a subgradient at the current iterate exactly when it satisfies the subgradient inequality for every point in the domain of the objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected best-value and iteration bound for stochastic projected subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded expected-gap and iteration guarantee obtained by invoking Theorem 8.35. Its hypotheses and the definitions of the constants are not expanded in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the hypotheses required to invoke Theorem 8.35, the stochastic projected subgradient method satisfies
\[
\mathbb{E}[f_{\mathrm{best}}^k]-f_{\mathrm{opt}}
\leq
\frac{\delta\sqrt{m}\,\sqrt{\left(\sum_{i=1}^m L_{f_i}^2\right)\sqrt{2\Theta}}}{\sqrt{k+2}}.
\]
In particular, for \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
N_2=\max\left\{\frac{2\delta^2m\Theta\sum_{i=1}^mL_{f_i}^2}{\varepsilon^2}-2,\,2\right\}
\]
iterations suffice to reach an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.35, the expected objective gap of the best stochastic projected-subgradient value obeys the displayed inverse-square-root bound. The displayed value N_2 is stated to suffice for epsilon-optimality in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \text{The hypotheses required to invoke Theorem 8.35 hold.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly convex stochastic projected-subgradient convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded expected objective-gap bounds for the best achieved value and a polynomially weighted average under strong convexity; the numbered assumptions are not expanded in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumptions 8.7 and 8.34 hold, \(\widetilde L_f>0\) is the constant specified in Assumption 8.34, and \(f\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex for some \(\sigma>0\). Let \(\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\) be generated by the stochastic projected subgradient method with
\[
t_k=\frac{2}{\sigma(k+1)}.
\]
Define
\[
f_{\mathrm{best}}^k=\min_{0\leq n\leq k}f(x^n).
\]
Then, for every \(k\geq0\),
\[
\mathbb{E}[f_{\mathrm{best}}^k]-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{2\widetilde L_f^2}{\sigma(k+1)}.
\]
For \(k\geq1\), define
\[
x^{(k)}=\sum_{n=0}^k\alpha_n^kx^n,
\qquad
\alpha_n^k=\frac{2n}{k(k+1)}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb{E}[f(x^{(k)})]-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{2\widetilde L_f^2}{\sigma(k+1)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 8.7 and 8.34, strong convexity with modulus sigma, and stepsizes 2 divided by sigma times k plus one, both the best achieved objective value and the stated polynomially weighted average have expected objective gap at most 2 times the square of the assumption constant divided by sigma times k plus one. The weighted average is defined only for k at least one.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde L_f>0\text{ is the constant specified in Assumption 8.34.}
\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by the stochastic projected subgradient method with }t_k=\frac{2}{\sigma(k+1)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Best-Value Convergence of Stochastic Projected Subgradient Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected convergence and an explicit compact-domain rate for best objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumptions 8.7 and 8.34 hold, and let \(\{\mathbf{x}^k\}_{k\ge0}\) be generated by the stochastic projected subgradient method with \(t_k>0\). Define
\[
f_{\mathrm{best}}^k=\min_{0\le n\le k}f(\mathbf{x}^n).
\]
If
\[
\frac{\sum_{n=0}^k t_n^2}{\sum_{n=0}^k t_n}\to0,
\]
then
\[
\mathbb{E}(f_{\mathrm{best}}^k)\to f_{\mathrm{opt}}.
\]
If additionally \(C\) is compact and
\[
\Theta\ge\max_{\mathbf{x},\mathbf y\in C}\frac12\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf y\|^2,
\qquad
t_k=\frac{\sqrt{2\Theta}}{\widetilde L_f\sqrt{k+1}},
\]
where \(\widetilde L_f\) is the conditional second-moment constant from Assumption 8.34, then for every \(k\ge2\),
\[
\mathbb{E}(f_{\mathrm{best}}^k)-f_{\mathrm{opt}}
\le\frac{2(1+\log 3)\,\widetilde L_f\sqrt{2\Theta}}{\sqrt{k+2}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 8.7 and 8.34, the expected best objective value converges to the optimum whenever the accumulated squared stepsizes are negligible relative to the accumulated stepsizes. On a compact feasible set, the stated inverse-square-root stepsizes give the displayed expected best-value error bound.
assumptions_latex: \text{For part (b): }C\text{ is compact and }\Theta\ge\max_{\mathbf{x},\mathbf y\in C}\frac12\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf y\|^2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb{E}(f_{\mathrm{best}}^k)\to f_{\mathrm{opt}};\quad\text{and under the part (b) hypotheses, }\mathbb{E}(f_{\mathrm{best}}^k)-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\le\frac{2(1+\log 3)\widetilde L_f\sqrt{2\Theta}}{\sqrt{k+2}}\ \forall k\ge2

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic-oracle conditions for the stochastic projected subgradient method.

\[

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Projected Subgradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic or prescribed-order component subgradient updates for finite-sum convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x)\) on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\). Choose \(x_1\in C\), positive stepsizes \((\alpha_t)\), and an index sequence \(i_t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), such as \(i_t=1+((t-1)\bmod m)\). At iteration \(t\), select \(g_t\in\partial f_{i_t}(x_t)\) and update \[x_{t+1}=P_C(x_t-\alpha_tg_t).\] One cycle consists of \(m\) consecutive component updates. After the prescribed number of updates or cycles, return a specified feasible iterate or an average of feasible iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process one convex component at a time, taking a projected component-subgradient step according to a cyclic or otherwise prescribed index sequence.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, convex, and subdifferentiable at generated points in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in C\) for all \(t\), while each update requires a subgradient of only the selected component \(f_{i_t}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incremental projected subgradient iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic cyclic component update for a finite-sum objective over C.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: x^0\in C;\quad \forall k\ge0:\ x^{k,0}=x^k,\ t_k>0,\quad x^{k,i+1}=P_C\!\left(x^{k,i}-t_k g^{k,i}\right),\quad g^{k,i}\in\partial f_{i+1}(x^{k,i})\ \ (i=0,\ldots,m-1),\quad x^{k+1}=x^{k,m}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from any point in C. At outer iteration k, choose a positive stepsize and cyclically take one projected subgradient step for each component f_1 through f_m; the final inner iterate becomes x^{k+1}.

knowledge_statements.title: Functional-Constraint Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Switching projected subgradient scheme for a convex objective subject to convex functional inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in C}f_0(x)\) subject to \(f_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. Choose \(x_1\in C\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_t\geq0\), and stepsizes \(\alpha_t>0\). If \(\max_i f_i(x_t)\leq\varepsilon_t\), choose \(g_t\in\partial f_0(x_t)\); otherwise choose an index \(i_t\) with \(f_{i_t}(x_t)>\varepsilon_t\) and \(g_t\in\partial f_{i_t}(x_t)\). Set \[x_{t+1}=P_C(x_t-\alpha_tg_t).\] Return a designated approximately feasible iterate or an average of objective-update iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use an objective subgradient at approximately feasible points and a violated-constraint subgradient otherwise, projecting every update onto the simple set.
assumptions_latex: \(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_m\) are proper convex functions subdifferentiable at generated iterates.
The violated constraint can be identified whenever the feasibility test fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate lies in \(C\), and each iteration targets either objective decrease or correction of a detected functional-constraint violation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Projected Subgradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient ascent on the concave Lagrange dual over nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex program \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)\leq0\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle\) and \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\) on \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Choose \(\lambda_1\geq0\) and \(\alpha_t>0\). At iteration \(t\), choose \(x_t\in\arg\min_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda_t)\), set \(s_t=h(x_t)\in\partial^+q(\lambda_t)\), and update \[\lambda_{t+1}=P_{\mathbb{R}_+^m}(\lambda_t+\alpha_ts_t).\] After \(T\) iterations, return a designated dual iterate and, when required, a weighted average of the primal minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ascend the concave dual function using constraint residuals from Lagrangian minimizers, projecting multipliers onto the nonnegative orthant.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian infimum is attained at each generated multiplier.
The dual function is finite at generated multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint objective and constraint-vector bounds for dual projected subgradient averages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded statement. The two averages are distinguished by their defining sums because the extract denotes both by the same symbol. The displayed norm is the raw norm \(\|g(x)\|_2\), not the positive-part violation norm \(\|[g(x)]_+\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
x_{\mathrm{full}}^{(k)}=\sum_{n=0}^{k}\mu_n^k x^n,
\qquad
x_{\mathrm{part}}^{(k)}=\sum_{n=\lfloor k/2\rfloor}^{k}\eta_n^k x^n.
\]
For every \(k\ge 2\) and \(\rho>0\),
\[
f(x_{\mathrm{full}}^{(k)})-f_{\mathrm{opt}}+\rho\|g(x_{\mathrm{full}}^{(k)})\|_2
\leq \frac{L}{2}\frac{(\|\lambda^0\|_2+\rho)^2+\sum_{n=0}^{k}\gamma_n^2}{\sum_{n=0}^{k}\gamma_n},
\]
and
\[
f(x_{\mathrm{part}}^{(k)})-f_{\mathrm{opt}}+\rho\|g(x_{\mathrm{part}}^{(k)})\|_2
\leq \frac{L}{2}\frac{(\|\lambda^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}\|_2+\rho)^2+\sum_{n=\lfloor k/2\rfloor}^{k}\gamma_n^2}{\sum_{n=\lfloor k/2\rfloor}^{k}\gamma_n}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 8.41 and the uniform bound on the constraint vector, the full and trailing-half primal averages generated by the dual projected subgradient method satisfy the displayed joint objective-gap and raw constraint-vector-norm bounds.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ and }\{\lambda^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ are generated by the dual projected subgradient method.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized dual projected subgradient algorithm for an LP over the simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-specific specialization of the dual projected subgradient method. As written, the normalized update requires a nonzero residual \(\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b\); the extract supplies no zero-residual convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min\{\mathbf c^T\mathbf x:\ \mathbf A\mathbf x\le\mathbf b,\ \mathbf x\in\Delta_n\},
\]
choose \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R_+^m\). For every \(k\ge0\), set
\[
\mathbf v=\mathbf c+\mathbf A^T\lambda^k,
\qquad i_k\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le n}v_i,
\qquad \mathbf x^k=\mathbf e_{i_k},
\]
and, whenever \(\|\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b\|_2>0\), update
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=
\left[
\lambda^k+ rac{1}{\sqrt{k+1}}
\frac{\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b}{\|\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b\|_2}
\right]_+.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a nonnegative multiplier. At iteration k, minimize the current Lagrangian coefficient vector over simplex vertices, use the selected unit vector as the primal response, and project onto the nonnegative orthant after a normalized residual step of length 1/√(k+1). The displayed normalization is defined only for a nonzero residual.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf c\in\mathbb R^n,\quad \mathbf A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad \mathbf b\in\mathbb R^m
\|\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b\|_2>0\ \text{for the displayed normalized update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i_k\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le n}(\mathbf c+\mathbf A^T\lambda^k)_i,\quad \mathbf x^k=\mathbf e_{i_k},\quad \lambda^{k+1}=\left[\lambda^k+\frac{\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b}{\sqrt{k+1}\,\|\mathbf A\mathbf x^k-\mathbf b\|_2}\right]_+

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual projected subgradient algorithm for network utility maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-utility specialization with separable source subproblems and componentwise projected link-price updates; no convergence claim or stepsize conditions are supplied in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the network utility maximization problem, initialize
\[
\lambda_\ell^0=0\qquad(\ell\in L).
\]
At each iteration \(k\), choose for every source \(s\in S\)
\[
x_s^k\in\arg\max_{x_s\in I_s}
\left\{u_s(x_s)-\left(\sum_{\ell\in L(s)}\lambda_\ell^k\right)x_s\right\},
\]
and update every link price by
\[
\lambda_\ell^{k+1}=
\left[
\lambda_\ell^k+
\alpha_k\left(\sum_{s\in S(\ell)}x_s^k-c_\ell\right)
\right]_+,
\qquad \ell\in L.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start all link prices at zero. At each iteration, each source independently maximizes its utility minus its aggregate route price over its allowed interval; each link then takes a step proportional to excess load and projects its price onto the nonnegative half-line.
assumptions_latex: \text{The network utility maximization data and incidence sets are as defined in the NUM model.}
(\alpha_k)_{k\ge0}\ \text{is the stepsize sequence used by the update}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standing Assumptions for the Dual Projected Subgradient Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete assumption package for the source's dual projected-subgradient framework, including convexity, primal attainment, strict feasibility, and attainment of every nonnegative-multiplier Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb E\) be convex; let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) and \(g_j:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\), be convex, with \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)^T\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The set X and all objective and constraint functions are convex; the primal value is finite and attained; a strictly feasible point exists; and every Lagrangian subproblem with a nonnegative multiplier attains its minimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected subgradient ascent for Lagrangian dual problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space projected ascent obtained from attained primal Lagrangian minimizers, with the stated convex-programming averaging setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\in X_0}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,p),\] define \[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,g(x)\rangle+\langle\mu,h(x)\rangle,\qquad L_D(\lambda,[0m\mu)=\inf_{x\in X_0}L(x,\lambda,\mu).\] The dual function is concave on \(\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\). If the infimum at \((\lambda^k,\mu^k)\) is attained at \(x^k\), then \((g(x^k),h(x^k))\) is a supergradient of \(L_D\), and the dual projected-subgradient update is \[\lambda^{k+1}=[\lambda^k+\tau_k\gamma_k g(x^k)]_+,\qquad \mu^{k+1}=\mu^k+\tau_k\gamma_k h(x^k).\] If additionally \(f\) and the \(g_i\) are convex, the \(h_j\) are affine, \(X_0\) is convex and compact, and Slater's condition holds, then the residual supergradients are uniformly bounded and one may choose \(\gamma_k=1\). The associated weighted primal averages are \[\bar x^\ell=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\tau_kx^k}{\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\tau_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian dual function is concave. A primal minimizer of the current Lagrangian supplies its constraint-residual supergradient; inequality multipliers take a projected ascent step and equality multipliers an unprojected ascent step. Under the stated convexity, compactness, and Slater assumptions, the residuals are uniformly bounded, unit scaling may be used, and weighted primal averages can be formed.
assumptions_latex: \text{For uniform boundedness and unit scaling: }f,g_i\text{ are convex},\ h_j\text{ are affine},\ X_0\text{ is convex and compact, and Slater's condition holds}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon-optimal and feasible primal solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded success criterion used locally in the dual projected subgradient analysis. This definition measures feasibility by the componentwise positive part of the constraint vector, unlike the raw norms displayed in the neighboring extracted rate statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon\geq0\) and the problem
\[
f_{\mathrm{opt}}=\min\{f(z):g(z)\leq0,\ z\in X\},
\]
a vector \(x\in X\) is called \(\varepsilon\)-optimal and feasible if
\[
f(x)-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\varepsilon
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\|[g(x)]_+\|_2\leq\varepsilon,
\]
where \([\cdot]_+\) is taken componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point in X is epsilon-optimal and feasible when its objective gap is at most epsilon and the Euclidean norm of its componentwise positive constraint violation is at most epsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-averaging rate for the dual projected subgradient method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded finite-iteration bounds for the full weighted primal average. The extract bounds the raw norm \(\|g(x)\|_2\). The constraint bound requires \(\alpha>0\) to be well-defined; the extract does not state this failure boundary explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
x_{\mathrm{full}}^{(k)}=\sum_{n=0}^{k}\mu_n^k x^n,
\qquad
\alpha=\frac{f(\bar x)-f_{\mathrm{opt}}}{\min_{1\leq j\leq m}\{-g_j(\bar x)\}},
\]
where \(\bar x\) is a Slater point. With \(\gamma_k=(k+1)^{-1/2}\), for every \(k\geq1\),
\[
f(x_{\mathrm{full}}^{(k)})-f_{\mathrm{opt}}
\leq \frac{L}{2}\frac{(\|\lambda^0\|_2+2\alpha)^2+1+\log(k+1)}{\sqrt{k+1}}.
\]
If additionally \(\alpha>0\), then
\[
\|g(x_{\mathrm{full}}^{(k)})\|_2
\leq \frac{L}{2\alpha}\frac{(\|\lambda^0\|_2+2\alpha)^2+1+\log(k+1)}{\sqrt{k+1}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With inverse-square-root stepsizes, the full primal average has an objective-gap bound of order log(k)/sqrt(k). When the Slater-derived parameter alpha is positive, the extract gives the same order for the raw constraint-vector norm.
assumptions_latex: \text{Assumption 8.41 holds, including existence of the stated Slater point }\bar x.
\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ and }\{\lambda^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ are generated by the dual projected subgradient method.}
\alpha=\frac{f(\bar x)-f_{\mathrm{opt}}}{\min_{1\leq j\leq m}\{-g_j(\bar x)\}};\quad \alpha>0\text{ is required for the constraint-norm estimate.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional complexity guarantee under the complete setting of Theorem 8.48; the quantities L, M, and α retain the meanings and hypotheses specified there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the setting of Theorem 8.48, let \(\varepsilon>0\). If \(k\ge 2\) and
\[
k\ge \frac{4L^2\bigl((M+2\alpha)^2+\log 3\bigr)^2}{\min\{\alpha^2,1\}\varepsilon^2}-2,
\]
then the partially averaged primal iterate \(\mathbf{x}^{(k)}\) satisfies
\[
f(\mathbf{x}^{(k)})-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\le \varepsilon,
\qquad
\|[\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}^{(k)})]_+\|_2\le \varepsilon.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under all hypotheses and definitions of Theorem 8.48, any iteration index k at least 2 and satisfying the displayed threshold yields a partially averaged primal iterate whose one-sided objective gap and positive-part constraint violation are both at most ε.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Dual Projected Subgradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic projected subgradient ascent on the nonnegative multiplier orthant, using constraint residuals obtained from exact Lagrangian subproblem minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). For each \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), choose \(\gamma_k>0\) and compute \[x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\lambda^k)^Tg(x)\}.\] If \(g(x^k)=0\), terminate and output \(x^k\). Otherwise set \[\lambda^{k+1}=\left[\lambda^k+\gamma_k\frac{g(x^k)}{\|g(x^k)\|_2}\right]_+,\] where \([\cdot]_+\) denotes projection onto \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from any nonnegative multiplier. At each iteration, exactly minimize the Lagrangian over the primal set. Stop if the constraint-residual vector is zero; otherwise take a normalized residual step in multiplier space and project it onto the nonnegative orthant.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Subgradient Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous projected descent-ascent for a convex-concave saddle formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty closed convex sets, and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). Choose \((x_1,y_1)\in X\times Y\) and \(\alpha_t>0\). At iteration \(t\), select \(g_t^x\in\partial_xL(x_t,y_t)\) and \(g_t^y\in\partial_y^+L(x_t,y_t)\), then update \[x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_tg_t^x),\qquad y_{t+1}=P_Y(y_t+\alpha_tg_t^y).\] After \(T\) iterations, return the weighted averages \(\bar x_T=(\sum_t\alpha_tx_t)/(\sum_t\alpha_t)\) and \(\bar y_T=(\sum_t\alpha_ty_t)/(\sum_t\alpha_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply projected subgradient descent to the primal variable and projected supergradient ascent to the dual variable, usually returning weighted averages.
assumptions_latex: \(L(\cdot,y)\) is proper convex on \(X\) and \(L(x,\cdot)\) is proper concave on \(Y\).
The displayed partial subgradients and supergradients exist at generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_t,y_t)\in X\times Y\) for every \(t\), and \((\bar x_T,\bar y_T)\in X\times Y\).

notation.meaning: subdifferential in the convex primal variable
superdifferential in the concave dual variable

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Iterate Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-selected output among finitely many feasible subgradient iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\in C\) be feasible iterates for minimizing a real-valued function \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\). A best-iterate output is any \[\widehat x_T\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\leq t\leq T} f(x_t).\] Equivalently, choose an index \(t_T^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\leq t\leq T}f(x_t)\) using a fixed tie-breaking rule and set \(\widehat x_T=x_{t_T^*}\). Then \(f(\widehat x_T)=\min_{1\leq t\leq T}f(x_t)\) and \(\widehat x_T\in C\). This output policy requires evaluating or otherwise comparing the objective values of the candidate iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return a generated feasible iterate having the smallest observed objective value, with a fixed rule for resolving ties.
assumptions_latex: Every \(x_t\) lies in \(C\) and every \(f(x_t)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T\in C\) and \(f(\widehat x_T)=\min_{1\leq t\leq T}f(x_t)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\geq 1\), let \(C\) be convex, let \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\in C\), and let weights \(w_t\geq 0\) satisfy \(W_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_t>0\). Define the ergodic output \(\bar x_T=W_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_tx_t\). For every convex function \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\), \[\bar x_T\in C,\qquad f(\bar x_T)\leq\frac{1}{W_T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_tf(x_t).\] More generally, let \(X\) and \(Y\) be convex, let \(x_t\in X\) and \(y_t\in Y\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\), define \(\bar x_T=W_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_tx_t\) and \(\bar y_T=W_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_ty_t\), and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in its first argument and concave in its second. Then, for every \((x,y)\in X\times Y\), \[L(\bar x_T,y)-L(x,\bar y_T)\leq\frac{1}{W_T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_t\bigl(L(x_t,y)-L(x,y_t)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted average of feasible iterates remains feasible, and convexity transfers averaged objective values to an objective bound at the average. For convex-concave saddle functions, explicitly defined primal and dual weighted averages satisfy the analogous averaged gap bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\geq1\), let \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\) belong to a convex set \(C\), and let \(w_1,\ldots,w_T\geq0\) with \(W_t=\sum_{s=1}^{t}w_s\) and \(W_T>0\). The weighted-average output is \[\bar x_T=\frac{1}{W_T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_tx_t.\] It is a convex combination of the generated iterates and hence belongs to \(C\). In projected subgradient methods, the stepsize-weighted choice \(w_t=\alpha_t\) yields \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha_t)\) whenever \(\alpha_t>0\). For every \(t\geq2\) such that \(W_{t-1}>0\), the output can be updated online by \[\bar x_t=\frac{W_{t-1}\bar x_{t-1}+w_tx_t}{W_t}.\] If initial weights vanish, initialize the recursion at the first index \(r\) with \(w_r>0\) by setting \(\bar x_r=x_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return a convex combination of generated iterates, commonly using stepsizes as weights. The average has an online recursion once the preceding cumulative weight is positive; if initial weights vanish, initialize it at the first positive-weight iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Output Weighting Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible weight sequences and standard regimes for finite ergodic outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iterates \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\), an admissible output-weighting regime specifies history-measurable weights \(w_t\geq0\) such that \(W_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_t>0\), and returns \(\bar x_T=W_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_tx_t\). Standard regimes include uniform weighting \(w_t=1\), stepsize weighting \(w_t=\alpha_t\), polynomial weighting \(w_t=t^p\) for \(p\geq0\), and terminal-window weighting \(w_t=\mathbf 1\{t\geq T-k+1\}\) for \(1\leq k\leq T\). If the iterates lie in a convex feasible set, every such regime produces a feasible output; convergence rates depend on matching the weights to the underlying per-iteration inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose nonnegative weights with positive total mass; common choices are uniform, stepsize, polynomial, or terminal-window weights.
assumptions_latex: The weights are determined without using future oracle information, except when a fixed terminal horizon defines a window.
At least one weight is positive.
All averaged iterates lie in a common convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed regime defines a convex-combination output \(\bar x_T\) in the same feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output rule for a finite Euclidean subgradient trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given iterates \(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_T\in C\) produced by a subgradient method and a prescribed horizon \(T\ge 1\), the last-iterate output policy returns \[\widehat{x}_T:=x_T.\] The policy performs no averaging, objective-value comparison, or additional oracle call. If the method is projected, feasibility of the output follows from \(x_T\in C\). This definition specifies only the reported point; any convergence guarantee for \(\widehat{x}_T\) requires assumptions and analysis tailored to last iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At horizon T, report the terminal iterate x_T without averaging, selecting a best point, or making another oracle call.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is the feasible set and \(x_t\in C\) for \(0\le t\le T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Suffix-Averaged Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-size-weighted averaging over a terminal suffix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0,\ldots,x_T\in C\), let \(m\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\), and let weights \(w_t\ge 0\) satisfy \(\sum_{t=m}^{T}w_t>0\). The suffix-averaged output beginning at \(m\) is \[\widehat{x}_{T,m}:=\frac{\sum_{t=m}^{T}w_t x_t}{\sum_{t=m}^{T}w_t}.\] In subgradient methods one commonly takes \(w_t=\alpha_t\), the step size used at iteration \(t\). Because the coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one after normalization, convexity of \(C\) implies \(\widehat{x}_{T,m}\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report a normalized weighted average of all iterates from a chosen suffix start m through the terminal index T.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(x_t\in C\) for \(m\le t\le T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Averaged Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform averaging over the last prescribed number of iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0,\ldots,x_T\in C\) and an integer tail length \(q\in\{1,\ldots,T+1\}\), define the tail index set \(I_{T,q}:=\{T-q+1,\ldots,T\}\). The tail-averaged output is \[\bar{x}^{\mathrm{tail}}_{T,q}:=\frac{1}{q}\sum_{t=T-q+1}^{T}x_t.\] Thus \(q=1\) recovers the last iterate, whereas \(q=T+1\) averages the entire trajectory. If \(C\) is convex and every retained iterate lies in \(C\), then \(\bar{x}^{\mathrm{tail}}_{T,q}\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report the uniform average of the final q iterates; q=1 gives the last iterate and q=T+1 gives the full average.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(x_t\in C\) for \(t\in I_{T,q}\).

children.title: Terminal Window Selection
children.top_down_role: Choices of starting index, window length, and horizon dependence for terminal averaging.

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Window Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility conditions for horizon-dependent terminal windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every horizon \(T\ge 1\), choose a start index \(m_T\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\) and define the terminal window \(I_T:=\{m_T,m_T+1,\ldots,T\}\), with length \(q_T:=T-m_T+1\). A terminal-window rule is asymptotically expanding and genuinely terminal when \[q_T\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad \frac{q_T}{T+1}\longrightarrow\rho\quad\text{for some }\rho\in[0,1].\] The case \(\rho>0\) retains a fixed asymptotic fraction of the trajectory; \(\rho=0\) permits a vanishing fraction while still requiring infinitely many retained iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a contiguous final window whose length diverges; its retained fraction may converge to a positive constant or vanish.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Distance Generators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong convexity relative to the norm used by mirror descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space equipped with norm \(\|\cdot\|\). A differentiable convex function \(h\) on an open convex set containing \(C\) is a \(\sigma\)-strongly convex distance-generating function on \(C\), where \(\sigma>0\), if for all \(x,y\in C\), \[h(x)\ge h(y)+\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x-y\|^2.\] Equivalently, its Bregman divergence satisfies \(D_h(x,y)\ge(\sigma/2)\|x-y\|^2\) on \(C\times C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distance generator is sigma-strongly convex when its linearization error dominates sigma/2 times the squared ambient norm distance.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and convex in a finite-dimensional normed space.
\(h\) is convex and differentiable on an open convex set containing \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Legendre Distance Generators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Legendre generators in the convex-analytic sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with \(U:=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\ne\varnothing\). The function \(h\) is a Legendre distance generator when it is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex: \(h\) is differentiable on \(U\), \(\|\nabla h(x_k)\|_*\to\infty\) whenever \(x_k\in U\) approaches a boundary point of \(\operatorname{dom}h\), and \(h\) is strictly convex on every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial h\). Its Bregman divergence is evaluated with second argument in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Legendre generator is a closed proper convex function that is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex on its effective domain.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h\) is Legendre precisely when it is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Legendre property and dual Bregman bound for a potential-generated regularizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of the separable regularizer generated by a zero-potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\psi\) be a \(0\)-potential and let \(F_\psi\) be its associated separable regularizer. Then \(F_\psi\) is Legendre. For all \(u,v\in\mathcal D^*=(-\infty,a)^d\) satisfying \(u_i\le v_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,d\), \[D_{F_\psi^*}(u,v)\le\frac12\sum_{i=1}^d\psi'(v_i)(u_i-v_i)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularizer generated by a zero-potential is Legendre. For coordinatewise ordered dual points, its conjugate Bregman divergence is bounded by a potential-weighted quadratic distance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Legendre Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracted definition of a Legendre distance generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R\) is Legendre when \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty with convex interior, \(F\) is strictly convex with continuous first partial derivatives throughout \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)\), and every sequence \((x_n)\subseteq\mathcal A\) converging to a boundary point of \(\mathcal A\) satisfies \(\|\nabla F(x_n)\|\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Distance Generators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise additive distance generators on product domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_n\) and write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\). A distance generator \(h:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is separable when there exist proper convex functions \(h_i:C_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that \[h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}h_i(x_i).\] At points where every \(h_i\) is differentiable, the generated divergence decomposes as \[D_h(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}D_{h_i}(x_i,y_i).\] Consequently, a Bregman proximal subproblem also separates coordinatewise whenever its feasible set and remaining objective term have the same product-additive structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable generator is a sum of coordinate functions; its Bregman divergence is the sum of their coordinatewise divergences.
assumptions_latex: \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_n\) is a product of convex sets.
\(h_i\) is proper and convex on \(C_i\) for every \(i\).
Each \(h_i\) is differentiable at the divergence base point.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Distance Generators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive generators aligned with a prescribed block decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_B\), let \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_B\), and write \(x=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(B)})\). A block distance generator has the form \[h(x)=\sum_{b=1}^{B}\lambda_b h_b\bigl(x^{(b)}\bigr),\qquad \lambda_b>0,\] where each \(h_b\) is a distance generator on \(C_b\). Wherever the block gradients exist, \[D_h(x,y)=\sum_{b=1}^{B}\lambda_b D_{h_b}\bigl(x^{(b)},y^{(b)}\bigr).\] The weights permit different geometric scaling across blocks while preserving additive Bregman structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block generator is a positively weighted sum of blockwise generators, yielding the same weighted sum of block Bregman divergences.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_b\) is differentiable at the divergence base point.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Divergence Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order linearization-error representation of Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be a proper convex function differentiable on an open convex set \(U\) in a finite-dimensional real vector space. For \(x,y\in U\), the Bregman divergence generated by \(h\) is \[D_h(x,y):=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle.\] Convexity gives \(D_h(x,y)\ge0\), and strict convexity gives \(D_h(x,y)=0\) only when \(x=y\). In general, \(D_h\) need not be symmetric and need not satisfy the triangle inequality, so it is a divergence rather than a metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is the gap between a convex function and its first-order affine approximation at the base point.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is open and convex in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(h\) is proper, convex, and differentiable on \(U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic properties of Bregman divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegativity, vanishing on the diagonal, and convexity in the first argument under differentiability at the second argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and let \(D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\nabla_{x-y}f(y)\). Then: (i) \(D_f(x,y)\ge 0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(y\in\operatorname{dom}(f)\); (ii) \(D_f(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}(f)\); and (iii) for every \(y\in\operatorname{dom}(\nabla f)\), the map \(x\mapsto D_f(x,y)\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is nonnegative and vanishes on the diagonal. When f is differentiable at the second argument, it is convex as a function of the first argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_f(x,y)\ge 0;\qquad D_f(x,x)=0;\qquad y\in\operatorname{dom}(\nabla f)\Rightarrow \bigl(x\mapsto D_f(x,y)\bigr)\text{ is convex}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(h:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with nonempty \(U:=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), and differentiable on \(U\). Provided the minimum is attained, the Bregman projection of \(y\) onto \(C\) is represented by \[P_C^h(y)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}D_h(x,y).\] If \(h\) is strictly convex on \(C\), the attained minimizer is unique. knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Quadratic Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic mirror geometry induced by a positive-definite linear metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, and define \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Hx\). Then \(\nabla\phi(x)=Hx\), \(\phi^*(y)=\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}y\), and \[D_\phi(u,v)=\tfrac12(u-v)^{\mathsf T}H(u-v)=\tfrac12\|u-v\|_H^2.\] Consequently, the Bregman projection of \(v\) onto a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) is the metric projection \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\|u-v\|_H^2\). For \(H=I\), this reduces to ordinary squared Euclidean distance and Euclidean projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic mirror map produces squared metric distance; its Bregman projection is exactly projection in that metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Geometry on the Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-entropy Bregman geometry on the probability simplex interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\sum_i x_i=1\}\) and define \(\phi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i\), with \(0\log0=0\). For \(v\in\operatorname{ri}(\Delta_n)\), \((\nabla\phi(v))_i=1+\log v_i\), and for \(u\in\Delta_n\), \[D_\phi(u,v)=\sum_{i=1}^n u_i\log\frac{u_i}{v_i},\] using \(0\log(0/v_i)=0\). The mirror-proximal update minimizing \(\eta\langle g,u\rangle+D_\phi(u,v)\) over \(\Delta_n\) is \[u_i^+=\frac{v_i e^{-\eta g_i}}{\sum_jv_j e^{-\eta g_j}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy generates Kullback–Leibler divergence on the simplex, and its linearized mirror step is the normalized multiplicative-weights update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\phi(u,v)=\sum_i u_i\log(u_i/v_i)\), with the displayed multiplicative update.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropy Prox Structure on a Simplex Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shifted negative-entropy prox functions on two probability simplices, paired with the ambient ℓ1 norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\Delta_n\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(u\in\Delta_m\subset\mathbb R^m\), define
\[
\|x\|_{\mathbb E_1}:=\sum_{i=1}^n|x^{(i)}|,\qquad
\|u\|_{\mathbb E_2}:=\sum_{j=1}^m|u^{(j)}|,
\]
and
\[
d_1(x):=\ln n+\sum_{i=1}^n x^{(i)}\ln x^{(i)},\qquad
d_2(u):=\ln m+\sum_{j=1}^m u^{(j)}\ln u^{(j)},
\]
with entropy terms on zero coordinates understood by continuous extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On each probability simplex, the ambient ℓ1 norm is paired with shifted negative entropy; entropy terms at zero coordinates are interpreted continuously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_1(x)=\ln n+\sum_{i=1}^n x^{(i)}\ln x^{(i)},\qquad d_2(u)=\ln m+\sum_{j=1}^m u^{(j)}\ln u^{(j)}

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Type Mirror Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable power potential and its coordinatewise mirror map on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(q>1\) and define \(\phi_q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(\phi_q(x)=q^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|^q\). Then \[(\nabla\phi_q(x))_i=|x_i|^{q-2}x_i,\qquad \phi_q^*(y)=\frac{1}{q^*}\sum_{i=1}^n|y_i|^{q^*},\] where \(q^*=q/(q-1)\) and every expression \(|s|^{r-2}s\) is assigned its continuous value \(0\) at \(s=0\). The inverse mirror map is \((\nabla\phi_q^*(y))_i=|y_i|^{q^*-2}y_i\), and \[D_{\phi_q}(u,v)=\frac1q\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(|u_i|^q-|v_i|^q-q|v_i|^{q-2}v_i(u_i-v_i)\bigr).\] Hence both the mirror map and its inverse act coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The separable q-power potential has a coordinatewise power gradient, a conjugate-exponent inverse map, and an explicit separable Bregman divergence, with the coordinate maps continuously defined as zero at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla\phi_q^*=(\nabla\phi_q)^{-1}\), with the displayed separable Bregman divergence.

knowledge_statements.title: p-Norm Mirror Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex squared-norm mirror potential for the regime \(1<p\leq2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p\leq2\) and define \(\psi_p(x)=\|x\|_p^2/[2(p-1)]\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). This function is \(1\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_p\). For \(x
eq0\), its mirror coordinate is \[(
abla\psi_p(x))_i= rac{\|x\|_p^{2-p}}{p-1}|x_i|^{p-2}x_i,\] with \(
abla\psi_p(0)=0\). Consequently, \[D_{\psi_p}(u,v)\geq rac12\|u-v\|_p^2.\] Its conjugate is \(\psi_p^*(y)=	frac{p-1}{2}\|y\|_{p^*}^2\), where \(p^*=p/(p-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For 1<p≤2, a scaled squared p-norm is one-strongly convex and gives explicit primal and dual mirror coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Power–Norm Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter conditions separating differentiability, strong-convexity, and dual-exponent behavior of power geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the separable power potential \(\phi_q(x)=\|x\|_q^q/q\), the mirror map is single-valued and continuous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) exactly in the differentiable regime \(q>1\), with conjugate exponent \(q^*=q/(q-1)\). For the squared-norm potential \(x\mapsto\|x\|_p^2/2\), the standard dimension-free strong-convexity estimate is \((p-1)\)-strong convexity relative to \(\|\cdot\|_p\) when \(1<p\leq2\); scaling by \(1/(p-1)\) makes the modulus one. At \(p=1\), differentiability and positive strong convexity fail, while for \(p>2\) this particular dimension-free quadratic lower bound is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power mirrors require exponent above one; squared p-norm geometry has the standard dimension-free strong-convexity normalization only for 1<p≤2.
assumptions_latex: Strong convexity is measured relative to the stated \(p\)-norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q>1\) ensures differentiability, while \(1<p\leq2\) yields the stated dimension-free squared-norm strong-convexity regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Entropy Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Von Neumann entropy geometry on positive-definite density matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D_d=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^d:\operatorname{tr}X=1\}\) and define \(\Phi(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\), with the continuous convention at zero. For \(Y\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal D_d)\), \(\nabla\Phi(Y)=\log Y+I\), and for \(X\in\mathcal D_d\), \[D_\Phi(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(X(\log X-\log Y)\bigr).\] For a symmetric direction \(G\) and \(\eta>0\), the entropy mirror step over \(\mathcal D_d\) is \[X^+=\frac{\exp(\log Y-\eta G)}{\operatorname{tr}\exp(\log Y-\eta G)}.\] No commutativity between \(Y\) and \(G\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Von Neumann entropy generates quantum relative entropy, and its mirror step is a trace-normalized matrix exponential update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\Phi(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(X(\log X-\log Y))\), with the displayed matrix-exponential update.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact three-point identity for a differentiable convex generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(\phi:U	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex. For all \(x,y,z\in U\), \[D_\phi(z,x)-D_\phi(z,y)-D_\phi(y,x)=\langle
abla\phi(y)-
abla\phi(x),z-yangle.\] Equivalently, \[\langle
abla\phi(y)-
abla\phi(x),y-zangle=D_\phi(z,y)+D_\phi(y,x)-D_\phi(z,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The difference of three Bregman divergences equals a gradient-difference pairing; reversing the pairing reverses the sign of the divergence difference.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Pythagorean Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman projection inequality for a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(C\subseteq U\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex. Fix \(x\in U\), and suppose \[y\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}D_\phi(u,x).\] Then \[\langle\nabla\phi(y)-\nabla\phi(x),z-y\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }\(z\in C\).\] Consequently, \[D_\phi(z,x)\geq D_\phi(z,y)+D_\phi(y,x)\qquad\text{for every }\(z\in C\).\] Equality holds for any \(z\in C\) for which the displayed optimality pairing is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman projection splits the divergence from any feasible comparison point into two divergence legs plus a nonnegative optimality residual.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in U\), and the displayed Bregman projection \(y\) exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Pythagorean Inequality for Bregman Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, interior membership, and the generalized Pythagorean inequality for projection onto a closed convex set intersecting the Legendre domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be Legendre on \(\overline{\mathcal D}\), and let \(\mathcal K\subseteq\overline{\mathcal D}\) be closed and convex with \(\mathcal K\cap\mathcal D\ne\varnothing\). For every \(x\in\mathcal D\), the point \(p=\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in\mathcal K}D_F(w,x)\) exists uniquely and belongs to \(\mathcal K\cap\mathcal D\). knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Comparison Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step comparison inequality for a composite Bregman proximal update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(U\subseteq X\) be open and convex, and let \(C\subseteq U\) be convex. Let \(h:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex. For \(x\in C\), \(g\in X^*\), and \(\eta>0\), suppose \[x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\left\{\eta\langle g,u\rangle+\eta h(u)+D_\phi(u,x)\right\}.\] Then every \(z\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}h\) satisfies \[\eta\bigl(\langle g,x^+-z\rangle+h(x^+)-h(z)\bigr)\leq D_\phi(z,x)-D_\phi(z,x^+)-D_\phi(x^+,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite Bregman proximal step bounds its linearized composite-objective gap by the decrease in comparison divergence minus the divergence of the step.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional, \(U\subseteq X\) is open and convex, and \(C\subseteq U\) is convex.
\(x\in C\), \(g\in X^*\), \(\eta>0\), and the displayed minimizer exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Telescoping Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summation rule converting one-step Bregman comparisons into endpoint and residual terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a positive integer, let \(U\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex. Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_{T+1},z\in U\), and suppose \(a_1,\ldots,a_T\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \[a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_t)-D_\phi(z,x_{t+1})-D_\phi(x_{t+1},x_t),\qquad t=1,\ldots,T.\] Then \[\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_1)-D_\phi(z,x_{T+1})-\sum_{t=1}^T D_\phi(x_{t+1},x_t).\] Since \(D_\phi\) is nonnegative, \[\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing the one-step Bregman comparisons cancels consecutive comparison divergences, leaving the initial-minus-final divergence and the cumulative nonnegative movement term.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is open and convex, and \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and convex.
The displayed one-step inequalities hold for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Geometry Ownership Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictability boundary for stochastic mirror-descent geometry selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_t\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[g_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\in\partial f(x_t)\). Standard stochastic mirror-descent conditioning applies when the selected geometry \(h_t\) and step size \(\eta_t\) are \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable. If \(h_t\) is instead chosen using the same realized \(g_t\) before forming the update, then the geometry-dependent iterate and divergence are generally correlated with the oracle noise; the conditional cancellation used in the usual analysis need not hold. Such a rule requires a separate coupled analysis, sample splitting, or an enlarged algorithmic model and cannot automatically inherit predictable-geometry guarantees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-step and cumulative mirror-step inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic mirror-step inequality under the source's context-defined divergence and prox geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_j\in\mathbb R^n, let v_1\in X^o, and for t=1,\ldots,j define v_{t+1}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle\zeta_t,x\rangle+V(v_t,x)\}. Then, for every x\in X and t=1,\ldots,j, \langle\zeta_t,v_t-x\rangle\le V(v_t,x)-V(v_{t+1},x)+\frac12\|\zeta_t\|_*^2. Moreover, for every x\in X, \sum_{t=1}^j\langle\zeta_t,v_t-x\rangle\le V(v_1,x)+\frac12\sum_{t=1}^j\|\zeta_t\|_*^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each mirror step bounds its linear discrepancy by a decrease in the source-defined divergence plus half the squared dual norm of the step vector. Summing the inequalities yields the cumulative bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact minimizer of a quadratic-over-linear stepsize bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar finite-horizon optimization used to select constant stepsizes in basic mirror-descent analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), \(\beta>0\), and an integer \(m\geq1\), the problem \[\min_{t_1,\ldots,t_m>0}\frac{\alpha+\beta\sum_{k=1}^m t_k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^m t_k}\] is solved by \[t_k=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{\beta m}},\qquad k=1,\ldots,m,\] and its optimal value is \[2\sqrt{\frac{\alpha\beta}{m}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive alpha and beta, the quadratic-over-linear finite-horizon bound is minimized by equal positive stepsizes, each equal to the square root of alpha divided by beta times m, and the minimum has the displayed value.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(C\subseteq E\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex. Let \(h\) be differentiable on an open set containing \(C\) and strongly convex on \(C\), choose \(x_1\in C\), and choose \(\eta_t>0\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\). At iteration \(t\), select \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\subseteq E^*\) and set \(x_{t+1}=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in C}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}\), where \(D_h(x,y):=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\). The closedness of \(C\), finite dimensionality, and strong convexity make this minimizer well-defined and unique. Return a declared last iterate or the declared step-size-weighted average \(\bar x_T:=(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t x_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained mirror descent linearizes the convex objective and uniquely minimizes that linearization plus a Bregman proximity term over the closed convex feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropic mirror-descent bound and Euclidean comparison on the simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-Euclidean simplex specialization and comparison with the corresponding Euclidean estimate; the quotient comparison requires a nonzero Euclidean bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, with \(\Delta_n\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). Endow \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(\|\cdot\|_1\), and apply mirror descent over \(\Delta_n\) using \(\omega(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i\), \(x^0=\tfrac1n e\), and appropriately chosen fixed-horizon stepsizes. With \(L_{f,\infty}=\max_{x\in\Delta_n}\|f'(x)\|_\infty\), \[f_{\mathrm{best}}^N-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\le \frac{\sqrt{2\log n}\,L_{f,\infty}}{\sqrt{N+1}}=:C_{\mathrm{ne}}^f.\] If \(C_{\mathrm e}^f=\sqrt2L_{f,2}/\sqrt{N+1}>0\) and \(\rho^f=C_{\mathrm{ne}}^f/C_{\mathrm e}^f\), then \[\frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{\sqrt n}\le \rho^f\le \sqrt{\log n}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropic mirror descent on the unit simplex has a best-value bound governed by the infinity norm of the subgradient and the square root of log n. When the Euclidean comparison bound is nonzero, the ratio of the two bounds lies between square root of log n divided by square root of n and square root of log n.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex.}
N\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\text{ and the fixed-horizon stepsizes are chosen appropriately.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_{\mathrm{best}}^N-f_{\mathrm{opt}}\le C_{\mathrm{ne}}^f:=\frac{\sqrt{2\log n}\,L_{f,\infty}}{\sqrt{N+1}};\qquad C_{\mathrm e}^f>0\Longrightarrow \frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{\sqrt n}\le\rho^f\le\sqrt{\log n}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose $x^0\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)$. For every $k=0,1,2,\ldots$, choose $t_k>0$ and $f'(x^k)\in\partial f(x^k)$, and set
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\left\langle t_k f'(x^k)-\nabla\omega(x^k),x\right\rangle+\omega(x)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize at a feasible point in the subdifferentiability domain of the mirror function. At each iteration, choose a positive stepsize and an objective subgradient, then minimize the resulting mirror-regularized linear model over the feasible set.
